title: Choose a rollout from the constraint
description: Select the release constraint that matters most. The active path shows the minimum mechanism that addresses it; select a component to inspect its responsibility.

nodes.label: Release owner
nodes.detail: Sets the exposure, owns the stop rule, and can pause or reverse the release without waiting for a code change.

nodes.label: Traffic router
nodes.detail: Directs requests to a selected version or environment. A fast routing change is the first recovery action for a bad release.

nodes.label: Stable version
nodes.detail: Continues serving compatible traffic while the candidate is observed. It is useful only if data and contracts remain compatible.

nodes.label: Candidate version
nodes.detail: Receives a bounded cohort, a rolling batch, a complete cutover, or shadow copies depending on the chosen strategy.

nodes.label: Health gate
nodes.detail: Compares candidate and stable technical and business signals against thresholds before a promotion can continue.

nodes.label: Standby environment
nodes.detail: Holds a production-like prior or candidate environment for a blue-green switch. It provides route reversal, not automatic data reversal.

scenarios.label: Downtime is acceptable
scenarios.summary: A planned maintenance window makes a recreate deployment viable: stop the old version, deploy the candidate, validate it, and restore the previous artifact if validation fails.
scenarios.result: Choose recreate only when the user-visible interruption is an accepted requirement. Its simplicity does not reduce the blast radius; it removes the old serving path during the change.

scenarios.label: Spare capacity is limited
scenarios.summary: The router keeps most traffic on healthy old instances while a batch of replacement instances becomes ready. Each batch must leave enough capacity for peak load and one failure.
scenarios.result: Choose a rolling update when the service can safely run mixed versions. Limit batch size, wait for readiness, and pause before the candidate reaches the whole fleet.

scenarios.label: Recovery must be near-instant
scenarios.summary: A complete standby environment is prepared and verified before the router switches traffic. The prior environment remains ready for an immediate route-back.
scenarios.result: Choose blue-green when route reversal matters more than duplicate runtime cost. Validate secrets, cache readiness, jobs, and data compatibility before the switch.

scenarios.label: Behavior is uncertain
scenarios.summary: The stable version remains the baseline while a small canary cohort or safe request mirror reaches the candidate. The health gate compares the two paths before exposure grows.
scenarios.result: Choose canary traffic for user-visible evidence and shadowing for safe comparison. Both require a representative cohort, versioned metrics, and an immediate route-back action.
